How a change applies

  • Change it in place. A switch for the staged packages, each extension and each MCP server, a chip for each tool, a picker for the model and the flow.
  • The flow picker is not the whole list. It leaves out what is in a skills folder, or in a repository not on this host, and any other name can be typed.
  • Nothing is written until you preview the change and confirm it.
  • A person, at the console. No tool reaches this action; dispatch_trigger_edit keeps today’s scope.
  • Undo puts back the keys the change touched, as they were. Where this page could not write them, the preview says so.

Trust model

This deployment's scheduler starts it on its schedule; an operator may fire it by hand. Each forge delivery is checked against its configured authentication, bot-loop guard, sender permissions and duplicate protection, then applicable quiet hours, image, repository protection and spend caps. Cron starts from the deployment schedule instead of a webhook. A comment may select another flow; only one comment trigger per forge may be declared.

Keeping a session continues its retained conversation on the same issue. Nothing merges by itself.

Before you change it

A job already in line keeps what it was queued with and runs without a change here, unless this trigger has gained a narrowing field the job lacks, such as a list of models, a cap or a server: then it is refused. Adding or deleting a row renumbers the rows after it.
